resale_co.name: Certificate of Occupancy (Resale / Rental)
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Lawnside Construction Office (Construction Code Department)
resale_co.lead_time: Allow 10 business days for the inspection to be completed
requirements: Working smoke alarm on each level and in every bedroom
CO alarm within 10 feet of sleeping areas
ABC extinguisher (2.5 lb) mounted within 10 feet of the cooking area (form still lists it)
Heater and roof certification from a NJ licensed contractor (resale only); a private home inspection or a new roof or heater under permit in the last 5 years is accepted instead
Heater/chimney connection secure; water heater relief valve pipe 2 to 6 inches from the floor
Sump pump may not discharge into the sewer line
Sidewalks and walkway to the house in good condition with no trip hazards
Graspable handrails on steps 24 inches or more above grade (both sides if 44 inches or wider); guardrails on decks and porches 24 inches or more above grade
GFCI outlets within 6 feet of sinks and along kitchen counters; all outlet and switch covers in place; no openings in the breaker panel
No water leaks; faucets working
Holes in walls and floors fixed; exposed wood painted inside and out
Trash and debris removed
House numbers visible from the street
All open construction permits completed and closed; no unresolved violation notices

fees.label: CO inspection, per unit (includes initial inspection and one re-inspection)
fees.quote: FEES: $75.00 Per Unit. Fee To Be Paid In The Form Of Cash, Check Or Money Order. The Fee Covers Initial Inspection and One (1) Re-Inspection.

fees.label: Additional re-inspection (after the included re-inspection, a missed re-inspection, or violations not fixed within 30 days)
fees.quote: If after the initial inspection and one (1) re, inspection, the applicant will be charged a re-inspection fee of $75.00.

fees.label: Fine for violations not corrected within 30 days, per day
fees.quote: Failure to complete violations within 30 days, may result in a $25 fine per day for the applicant for each and every day the violation continues.

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Certificate of Occupancy Application (circle Resale) and submit it to the Construction Office, 4 Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Road, with $75 per unit in cash, check or money order. Choose pick up, fax or email for the certificate. Repairs must be done within 30 days of the first inspection or a new application is needed.

evidence.quote: It shall be unlawful to use or permit the use of any structure or building or part of the structure or building that presently exists in the Borough of Lawnside or any structure or building that has had a change in ownership or a change in occupancy, if that portion of the structure has been leased or sold, until a certificate allowing the new occupancy and/or use shall have been applied for by the owner or the owner's agent and such certificate issued by the Construction Code Official.
evidence.doc_date: Code 53-5, added 5-5-2004 by Ord. No. 07-FY2004; fees amended 12-7-2022 by Ord. No. 14-2022 (ecode360, legislation through 06-03-2026)

evidence.quote: NOTE: This Dwelling Is Not To Be Occupied Until A Cerificate Of Occupancy Is Issued By The Construction Code Department Of The Borough Of Lawnside.
Please Allow Ten (10) Business Days For Inspection To Be Completed.
All Work That Is Related To Open Construction Permits Must Be Completed And Permit Closed Out Prior To The Issuance Of A Certicate Of Occupancy.
A Heater and Roof Certification (Resale Only) must be provided by a NJ. Licensed Contractor.
PRIMARY CONTACT: Email Marian Hauser m.hauser@lawnside.net

resale_co.notes: Re-checked October 20, 2026. The Borough code on ecode360 (Chapter 53, section 53-5, read in full through the print view) requires a certificate of occupancy or certificate of continued occupancy after any change of ownership, applied for by the owner or owner's agent and issued by the Construction Code Official; repairs needed for the certificate are the current owner's responsibility. Code 53-5B (Ord. No. 14-2022) sets the same $75 per unit fee (initial inspection plus one reinspection), $75 extra reinspection and $25 per day violation fine as the application, so those are not listed twice. Inspections follow the 2015 International Property Maintenance Code (the code text cites BOCA 1993) and are visual only. The CO application is dated December 2022 and is still linked from the Borough site. The Construction Department page now shows only the email lawnsideinspections@lawnside.net; the phone (856) 573-6214 and Marian Hauser's email come from the application. Code 109 also offers an optional $25 informational inspection or status report for a prospective purchaser; that is not the resale CO. Rental properties also need a Landlord Mercantile License and Rental Unit Registration (rental program).
resale_co.contact_title: Primary contact named on the Construction Office CO application

requirements: All smoke alarms (hardwired and battery) must be less than 10 years old; take them down and check the date, replace if undated
Smoke alarm type by build year: pre-1975 homes need 10-year sealed battery alarms on each level including the basement; newer homes need AC powered, interconnected alarms per the year-built chart
Borough Code 70-6B(4): a working smoke detector and CO detector in each sleeping area, plus one outside each sleeping area within 10 feet
CO alarm outside of but within 10 feet of all sleeping areas if there is a fuel-burning appliance, fireplace or garage; CO alarms must be less than 7 years old
Low-voltage alarm systems must be tested by an alarm contractor before the inspection, with the certificate shown to the inspector
House numbers: Arabic numerals at least 3 inches, contrasting, at least 60 inches above ground, visible from the street
Homes with a secondary power source (solar, generator, battery storage) need a printed label within 18 inches of the main panel and meter, like "CAUTION MULTIPLE SOURCES OF POWER"
Fire extinguisher (form still lists it on the June 2025 version posted by Lawnside, and Code 70-6B still names extinguisher inspections): fully charged 2-A:10-BC in or within 10 feet of the kitchen

authorities.name: Regional Fire Prevention Alliance (Borough of Barrington Bureau of Fire Prevention)
authorities.area_served: Serves Barrington, Hi-Nella, Lawnside, Mt. Ephraim and Oaklyn; covers the entire borough
authorities.lead_time: Lowest fee with 14 or more business days notice before the change of occupant (weekends, holidays and the settlement date do not count). The Alliance form says certificates are valid 6 months; Borough Code 70-6B(3) says 90 days.

fees.label: Request received 14+ business days before change of occupant
fees.quote: 14+ business days prior to the change of occupant is $66.00.

fees.label: Request received 8 to 13 business days before
fees.quote: 8-13 business days prior to the change of occupant is $74.00.

fees.label: Request received 4 to 7 business days before
fees.quote: 4-7 business days prior to the change of occupant is $106.00.

fees.label: 3 business days or less notice
fees.quote: 3 business days or less notice prior to change of occupant is $171.00.

fees.label: Re-inspection after a failed inspection
fees.quote: ALL FAILED INSPECTIONS WILL REQUIRED A $50.00 RE INSPECTION FEE.

authorities.how_to_apply: Fill out the Alliance's certificate application and email it to firealliance@barringtonboro.com, or print it and drop it in the mailbox or mail it to 205 Haines Avenue, Barrington, NJ 08007. A check or money order payable to 'Regional Fire Prevention Alliance' must go with the application. Fees are non-refundable.

fire_cert.notes: Lawnside's own code (Chapter 70, read on ecode360) names the Regional Fire Prevention Alliance as the local enforcing agency and sets the same resale smoke/CO fees as the Alliance form ($66 / $74 / $106 / $171 and a $50 reinspection), so the code amounts are not listed twice. Validity conflict: the Alliance's November 2025 form says certificates are valid 6 months; Code 70-6B(3) says 90 days. The November 2025 form on the Alliance page has no extinguisher section (in line with P.L.2025, c.19) and states a $500 penalty; the June 2025 version posted on Lawnside's site (scanned, not machine-readable) includes extinguisher rules and a $600 penalty. The Borough CO checklist separately asks for a 2.5 lb ABC extinguisher within 10 feet of the cooking area. Walk-in office hours Tuesday to Friday 8am to 2pm; inspections Monday to Friday 9am to 2pm. DCA fire directory lists Fire Official Nicholas D'Alonzo (ndalonzo@barringtonboro.com) with an SSA with Barrington Borough.

other_items.label: Open permits must be closed
other_items.detail: All work under open construction permits must be completed and permits closed before the CO is issued.

other_items.label: Heater and roof certification (resale only)
other_items.detail: From a NJ licensed contractor, or a private home inspection, unless a new roof or heater was installed under a UCC permit in the last 5 years.
